title: Alphabet Board Path Problem

constraints: target consists only of English lowercase letters.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]
content.problemStatement:
On an alphabet board, we start at position `(0, 0)`, corresponding to character `board[0][0]`.

Here, `board = ["abcde", "fghij", "klmno", "pqrst", "uvwxy", "z"]`, as shown in the diagram below.

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2019/07/28/azboard.png)

We may make the following moves:

* `'U'` moves our position up one row, if the position exists on the board;
* `'D'` moves our position down one row, if the position exists on the board;
* `'L'` moves our position left one column, if the position exists on the board;
* `'R'` moves our position right one column, if the position exists on the board;
* `'!'` adds the character `board[r][c]` at our current position `(r, c)` to the answer.

(Here, the only positions that exist on the board are positions with letters on them.)

Output a sequence of moves that makes our answer equal to `target` in the smallest number of moves.  You may output any path that does so.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: target = "leet"
Output: "DDR!UURRR!!DDD!"
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: target = "code"
Output: "RR!DDRR!UUL!R!"
```

**Constraints:**

* `1 <= target.length <= 100`
* `target` consists only of English lowercase letters.

hidden.label: Transition to final letter of row 2

notes: Each character transition uses the minimum Manhattan number of moves.
The chosen ordering avoids nonexistent cells on the irregular z row.
solution.approach: Map each lowercase letter to its fixed board coordinate. For each target character, move up first, then left, then right, then down, and append !. The up/left-first order is necessary around z because the final row contains only z.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) for the returned path, with O(1) auxiliary state.

bruteForce.complexity: O(n) on the fixed-size graph, with unnecessary search overhead.
bruteForce.description: Treat the 26 valid cells as a graph and search for a shortest path for every target character. This is correct but unnecessary on the fixed board.

better.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) output space.
better.description: Precompute coordinates for the 26 letters and emit the Manhattan path between consecutive characters, taking care around z.

optimal.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) output space; O(1) auxiliary state.
optimal.description: Compute each character coordinate directly with division and modulo, emit U/L before D/R, then append !.

hints: Map each letter to coordinates using its alphabet index.
Compare current and target rows and columns to determine movement.
When z is involved, move upward/leftward before downward/rightward.
Append ! only after reaching the target character.
followUps: Why must movement ordering be careful around z?
How would this change if the board were arbitrary input?
How would a rectangular board differ?
learningObjectives: Construct shortest paths with Manhattan distance.
Handle an irregular final row safely.
